scope.q: What specific criteria or business metrics define a 'ticket that matters' beyond just volume, and how are these currently (if at all) being tracked or measured?
scope.why: Understanding the true definition of 'mattering' is critical to building a solution that aligns with business value, not just a generic prioritization.

scope.q: What are the existing data sources for customer tickets (e.g., Zendesk, Salesforce Service Cloud, custom CRM) including their schema, access methods, and typical data completeness?
scope.why: Knowing the precise data landscape is fundamental for ingestion, processing, and integration, and directly impacts technical feasibility and complexity.

scope.q: What is the acceptable latency and desired frequency for ticket prioritization updates, and what is the current workflow for ticket assignment and escalation?
scope.why: Defining the operational window and integration points is crucial for designing a system that fits into existing support processes without disruption and meets user expectations.

decomposition.title: Data Ingestion & Preprocessing
decomposition.why: This establishes the foundation by reliably pulling raw ticket data and transforming it into a usable format for analysis.

decomposition.title: Feature Engineering & Labeling
decomposition.why: This step extracts relevant signals from the raw data and defines what 'mattering' looks like for the model.

decomposition.title: Prioritization Model Training & Evaluation
decomposition.why: This focuses on building and validating the core AI logic that determines ticket importance.

decomposition.title: Prediction & Scoring Service
decomposition.why: This component serves the trained model, providing real-time prioritization scores for new and updated tickets.

decomposition.title: Integration with Support System
decomposition.why: This ensures the prioritized information is seamlessly delivered back into the customer support team's workflow.

sprint.title: Set up Data Ingestion Pipeline
sprint.deliv: Working script to pull 1000 tickets from customer's CRM and store in a local database.

sprint.title: Define & Extract Initial Features
sprint.deliv: Python script that extracts basic features (e.g., word count, sender domain) from raw tickets.

sprint.title: Build & Train Baseline Model
sprint.deliv: A simple classification model (e.g., Logistic Regression) trained on initial features, reporting F1 score.

sprint.title: Develop Prediction Service API
sprint.deliv: REST API endpoint that accepts ticket data and returns a priority score using the baseline model.

sprint.title: Integrate with Support System (Read-only)
sprint.deliv: A dashboard or simple UI that displays the top 10 prioritized tickets from the prediction service.

sprint.title: Refine Features and Retrain
sprint.deliv: Improved model with additional features (e.g., NLP embeddings), demonstrating higher F1 score.

sprint.title: User Acceptance Testing & Feedback
sprint.deliv: Support team reviews the prioritized list and provides structured feedback on accuracy and utility.

risks.risk: Ambiguous definition of 'ticket that matters' leads to a model that prioritizes irrelevant tickets.
risks.mitigation: Conduct extensive interviews with support managers and agents to establish clear, quantifiable metrics for 'mattering' (e.g., churn risk, revenue impact, regulatory compliance) and iterate on labels.

risks.risk: Poor quality or incomplete historical ticket data makes it impossible to train an effective model.
risks.mitigation: Perform a thorough data audit upfront, identifying gaps and inconsistencies. Implement data cleaning and imputation strategies, or suggest a manual labeling effort for a subset of critical tickets if automated methods fail.

risks.risk: Lack of clear feedback loop from support agents on model accuracy leads to low adoption and distrust.
risks.mitigation: Implement a 'thumbs up/down' or 'correct/incorrect' feedback mechanism within the support UI, allowing agents to easily flag mis-prioritized tickets to continuously improve the model.

risks.risk: Integrating the prioritization scores back into the existing CRM/helpdesk system is complex or requires significant changes.
risks.mitigation: Start with a read-only integration (e.g., a separate dashboard or prioritized list) to validate value. Then, explore native API capabilities of the CRM for direct updates, or develop a lightweight custom plugin if necessary, clearly outlining integration costs.
